candidates.source_title: Council staff will no longer be out of pocket when receiving backpay, says union - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Staff at Rochdale Council who receive Universal Credit will soon be able to have backpay staggered to limit the impact on their benefits when they get a wage rise, the union Unison has confirmed.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Staff at Rochdale Council who receive Universal Credit will soon be able to have backpay staggered to limit the impact on their benefits when they get a wage rise, the union Unison has confirmed. By 2027, all council employees will have the option of receiving the extra as a lump sum or in staggered amounts. The change, agreed by the council, follows a petition organised by school support workers and signed by more than 900 people. Previously, the council only paid backpay as a lump sum. That meant it was treated as additional income for Universal Credit recipients and resulted in benefit payments being reduced or stopped the following month. In some cases, student loan repayments could also be affected, says Unison. The new system will allow staff to spread backpay across Universal Credit assessment periods, helping to limit the financial blow. READ MORE: Historic mill to be turned into apartments Joanne, a teaching assistant in Rochdale, said that on one occasion, she lost more than £350 from her monthly Universal Credit payment. She said: “As a parent, the previous arrangements created a huge budgeting problem. The reduction often happened in January, just after Christmas when money was already tight, so I had to make sure I’d put money aside.”

candidates.source_title: Simister Island overnight closures planned
candidates.source_summary: Simister Island on the M60 will be closed overnight this week and next week as part of the major works on the junction.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Tonight (August 26), from 9pm until 6am, junction 18 will be shut. The same overnight closures will also take place tomorrow (August 27), September 1 and September 2.

National Highways made the decision to avoid these closures over the bank holiday weekend, according to their website. Diversion routes will be put in place for those passing through.

These works form part of the major interchange upgrade, currently estimated to be completed by 2030. The project will see five lanes of traffic and a new link road will be created at Junction 18 in a bid to ease congestion, following official confirmation by the Department for Transport (DfT) last year.

Simister Island interchange, which connects the M60, M62 and M66 motorways, is notorious for being one of the North West’s busiest motorway junctions. The scheme – estimated to cost between £255m and £296m – aims to reduce congestion, improve journey times and create a safer route.

The junction is used by around 90,000 vehicles each day, according to National Highways.

The project itself will see a ‘northern loop’ built to stop thousands of vehicles using the current traffic light controlled roundabout every day. A five-lane section on both sides of the M60 between Prestwich and Simister (junctions 17 and 18) has been touted as well.

The M66 on the Bury side of the junction would also be widened with new lanes introduced at the interchange and a second lane added from the M60 northbound link.

National Highways said: “Simister Island Interchange is one of the busiest motorway junctions in the north-west used by around 90,000 vehicles each day. The junction struggles with such high volumes of traffic above what it was designed for, and as a result suffers from congestion and poor journey time reliability.

“The project will improve junction 18 of the M60 and facilitate smoother flows of traffic along the connecting motorways, contributing to more reliable and safer journeys into and around Greater Manchester.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A local football club has installed new facilities to support fans recovering from cancer A local football club has installed new dedicated health facilities to help support supporters living with medical conditions. The major stadium upgrade makes the venue far more accessible for male fans recovering from life-saving cancer treatment. A total of 26 specially designed male incontinence bins have been put into action across the ground's rest areas. Statistically, one in eight men will get prostate cancer during their lifetime, with 60 per cent of those treated experiencing incontinence. The Crown Oil Arena can seat more than 9,000 supporters, meaning more than 1,100 male fans attending could be diagnosed with the illness. By introducing the new units, the club has earned a bronze award under the national BOG STANDARD charter scheme. Richard Knight, club director, commented: “Inclusion is important to us at the Club, and we didn’t ever want to think of any of our fans being unable to join, just because we didn’t have sanitary bins in place for them.”

candidates.source_title: Energy Secretary responds to Ofgem's £60 a year energy price cap increase
candidates.source_summary: Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has made a statement regarding Ofgem's announcement of the next energy price cap which is to take effect in October of this year, costing the average household £60 a year
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Fahnbulleh said: 'Families will be understandably concerned about the cost of energy bills this winter, which is being driven up by the Iran War.  

'Energy is an everyday essential and it needs to be affordable for everyone, which is why we have cut VAT on electricity bills from October, to give families some breathing space.  

'This has limited the rise in the price cap and follows the £150 in costs we removed from bills earlier this year, and we will keep looking at what more we can do to protect families from unaffordable bills.'

The price cap announced by Ofgem is a rise of 4%, a three-year high, costing the average household around £5 a month, equating to £60 a year. This comes after Andy Burnham announced the removal of VAT from electricity bills, and the speculation around whether Burnham will begin drilling in the North Sea.

The Iran War began on 28 February 2026, with US-Israeli strikes killing numerous senior Iranian officials, including the Iranian Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. This instigated the still ongoing war between allies America and Israel against Iran, that has led to the Strait of Hormuz, a key area regarding the movement of oil, located at the southern border of Iran, undergoing immense disruption, drastically decreasing the amount of maritime traffic in the area.

The Strait of Hormuz, prior to the war, carried roughly 20% of the world's petroleum consumption according to Times Now, with around 130 ships making journeys through the Strait of Hormuz daily. Due to the disruptions, including the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, oil and energy prices have risen across the globe, with the pre-war baseline for Brent crude oil being around $72 a barrel, which jumped to almost $120 at its peak. Today, the price of a barrel of Brent crude is $86.27. This has declined from the $100 spike just over a month ago for a barrel of Brent crude.

The reverberations of the catastrophic consequences of the Iran War have been felt on energy bills across the country, with the BBC reporting that the 'typical' bill will rise to £1862, which would be a rise of £221 a year.

However, Fahnbulleh was asked on LBC if the rise in bills was solely due to the ongoing wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine, or if government policy regarding renewable subsidies also has been contributing to the rise in energy bills. The Energy Secretary responded saying that 'it is both'. She later said that 'for the grid to operate properly, we've got to upgrade it', blaming the previous government for a lack of investment in the energy grid over their 14 years in power. Ofgem have said that household energy bills would have been £45 higher per year if Andy Burnham had not removed VAT from electricity bills.

candidates.source_title: The Margaret Haes Riding Centre celebrates 60th anniversary
candidates.source_summary: The event was attended by James Frith, MP for Bury North, Cllr Mohammed Tahir Rafiq, Mayor of Bury, and David Catterall, Deputy Lieutenant for Greater Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The Margaret Haes Riding Centre celebrated their 60th anniversary with an award ceremony, the unveiling of a plaque for George Lomax, ridden displays to music, and a performance from the Greater Manchester North Rock Choir.

The charity focuses on delivering services to those with physical or mental disabilities, and emotional or social challenges, bringing the 'Spirit of the Horse' to the most vulnerable in society.

They rely solely on volunteers to run the charity, with their proclaimed purpose being to 'empower children and adults with learning disabilities, physical and mental health disabilities, and emotional and social challenges; to lead active, healthy and fulfilling lives through equestrian activities,' and 'to have a positive impact on the health and well-being for all our riders and volunteers.'

In a social media post, James Frith, MP for Bury North said 'The centre is such an important part of our community in Bury North. It helps children and adults lead active and fulfilling lives, build confidence and communication skills, and provides vital support for people with disabilities.'

On their website, the centre has a plethora of stories from those who have gone to the Margaret Haes Riding Centre, either as a recipient of their services or as a volunteer, sharing their positive experiences and how that place has helped them and/or their family and friends.

For 60 years, the Margaret Haes Riding Centre has provided equine care, and social connection with local individuals through horses across the West Pennine Moors in the Holcombe area of Bury, the celebration of their anniversary on the 15th was described by James Frith MP as 'a thank you to everyone who has supported the centre over the years.'

candidates.source_summary: The second part of an historic mill in Rochdale will be turned into apartments.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The second part of an historic mill in Rochdale will be turned into apartments. Home Grace Co Ltd has been granted permission by Rochdale Council to turn commercial units on the ground floor of Sudden Mill in Manchester Road into three apartments. It follows planning permission granted to turn the first floor into five apartments. The mill was previously occupied by the Homegrace Outlet, which sold pillows and bedding. The site is next to Sudden Brook and close to the roundabout with Manchester Road, Bolton Road and Silk Road. Sudden Mill is included on the council’s register of non-designated heritage assets which does not allow for any external changes to be made without planning permission. The earliest Ordnance Survey maps of the area show the site as open space in the 1840s, likely to have been agricultural land. By the 1890s, the site was occupied by the Littlefields Cotton Mill. It had 320 looms, manufacturing T-cloths, flanelettes and other material.

They went on to record their seminal track, Atmosphere, at Cargo Studios in Kenion Street, Rochdale, before tragedy struck. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A jury in the trial of six men accused of historic sexual offences allegedly committed against three girls in Rochdale has been sworn in. Tahir Rashid, 55, Mohammed Saleem, 47, Sucklane Shah, 47, Amjad Mahmood, 54, Iftaq Hussain, 46, and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. Their trial at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester is due to begin tomorrow, (August 26) when jurors are set to hear the prosecution’s opening speech. The complainants are referred to as Girl A, Girl B and Girl C for legal reasons. Jurors have heard that Mr Mahmood is unfit to stand trial and is not present in the dock. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter Judge Matthew Corbett-Jones told the jury that he is ‘in hospital outside of the country receiving treatment for a complex psychiatric illness’. He told jurors that in due course, instead of the standard guilty or not guilty verdict, they will have to consider whether he ‘committed the alleged act’ and also ‘whether he did so in circumstances where the alleged complainant didn’t consent to the penetration’. The judge also told jurors that he would ‘strongly discourage’ them from setting up a group chat between themselves. While he said some juries set up group chats to discuss logistic issues, he warned them that material discussing the case in such a group would be prohibited. The judge said: “Anything being exchanged within that group about the case itself is something which would be prohibited by the rules.” A jury of 12 people and two alternate jurors were sworn in today (August 25). Mr Mohammed, of Merefield Street, Rochdale, denies four counts of rape and one count of assault by penetration. The charges include allegations against Girl A and Girl B. candidates.source_title: Masdar expands UK battery storage portfolio with new Rochdale project - Fast Company Middle East
candidates.source_summary: The facility marks the latest step in Masdar’s AED5 billion UK battery storage investment program and will provide enough clean power for 35,000 homes a day.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Abu Dhabi-based renewable energy company Masdar has started commercial operations at its second battery energy storage system (BESS) project in the UK, advancing its AED5 billion ($1.36 billion) investment program aimed at strengthening the country’s energy security and renewable energy infrastructure. Located in Rochdale, the 35MW/70MWh facility can provide enough clean power for 35,000 homes per day, based on two charging and discharging cycles. The project will also provide grid-balancing services, responding to fluctuations in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds to support grid stability. The launch follows Masdar’s acquisition of Arlington Energy in 2022, after which the company committed to developing a 3GWh pipeline of battery storage projects across the UK. The portfolio is expected to support the integration of more renewable energy into the UK electricity system by storing power during periods of lower demand and releasing it when demand increases. Masdar’s investment also aligns with the UK government’s Clean Power 2030 Action Plan, which targets up to 27GW of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade. “Beginning commercial operations at our Rochdale facility is a key milestone in our £1 billion ($1.36 billion) commitment to UK battery storage,” said Husain Al Meer, Executive Director, Global Offshore Wind & UK at Masdar. “As electricity demand grows and renewable generation continues to expand, battery storage is becoming an increasingly vital component of maintaining a secure, reliable and affordable electricity network,” he added. The Rochdale facility follows Masdar’s 20MW/40MWh Welkin Road battery storage project in Stockport, which began commercial operations last December. Masdar is also developing BESS projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, with a combined capacity of 150MW/300MWh. The company recently secured up to AED485.8 in financing from SMBC and ING for the four UK projects.

candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Abu Dhabi Future Energy Co PJSC (Masdar) has begun commercial operations at a 35-megawatt (mW) battery energy storage system (BESS) in Rochdale, England, its second start-up toward a target of three-gigawatt-hour (gWh) BESS capacity across the United Kingdom.

At 70 megawatt hours (mWh), the new facility can provide clean power for 35,000 homes a day, according to the Emirati state-owned company.

"The facility will also provide critical grid balancing services, responding to fluctuations in supply and demand within milliseconds to help maintain a secure and reliable electricity network", Masdar said in a press release Monday.

"BESS solutions are critical to integrating renewables into modern electricity networks, providing flexible energy to the grid by storing energy in periods of low demand and releasing it at peak times", it said.

Masdar set a goal to build one of the biggest BESS portfolios in the UK after acquiring Arlington Energy Ltd in 2022. It has earmarked GBP 1 billion (around $1.36 billion) for the target, as announced by the company February 27, 2024.

Late last year, Masdar put into service its first BESS project in the UK, the 20-mW/40-mWh Welkin Road project in Stockport, England, as announced by the company December 17, 2025.

It is developing more BESS projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff that will have a combined capacity of 150 mW/300 mWh. Last month Masdar said on social media it had completed GBP 97 million in financing for the two projects and the now completed Rochdale project.

candidates.source_title: Tougher laws could restrict use of fireworks - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Loud fireworks could be restricted to professional displays under plans being considered to tackle anti-social behaviour and reduce the risk of wildfires
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Loud fireworks could be restricted to professional displays under plans being considered to tackle anti-social behaviour and reduce the risk of wildfires. When the government issued a UK-wide fire alert earlier this month, it imposed a temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues and encouraged people not to do anything that could start fires, including using firepits, garden incinerators and fireworks. At the time, many people called for the ban to be extended to include the sale fire works which they felt posed a serious fire risk, as well as a nuisance. Now the government is giving people the chance to have their say with proposed changes including restricting the loudest pyrotechnics to professional display. The issue has been highlighted by Rochdale MP Paul Waugh who has been contacted by dozens of residents about fireworks being set off near homes and late at night. Mr Waugh said: “Fireworks have been a real worry for many of you across Rochdale and our villages — the noise, the late nights, and the distress to pets and veterans. “Now there’s a chance to change the rules. The Government is consulting on limiting the loudest fireworks to professional displays, and it’s open until October 7. “I’ve also written to ministers about the growing wildfire risk, and I’m working with the council on local enforcement.

candidates.source_summary: Crawley bag first win of season with victory at Rochdale Ayr Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Crawley Town got their League Two season up and running with a 2-1 win at Rochdale. The Red Devils, who only escaped relegation on the final day of last season, had lost their opener at home to Crewe when they finished with nine men. Crawley went ahead in the eighth minute through Peterborough loanee Pemi Aderoju, who fired home from a left-wing cross by Osman Kamara, his first goal for the club, as they were the more dangerous side in the opening half. Dale started the second period strongly and equalised in the 54th minute when centre back Ethan Ebanks-Landell headed home Ryan East’s header at the far post, only his seventh goal for the club in 154 matches. However, Crawley regained the lead in the 72nd minute through Louie Watson’s penalty after a trip by Kaiden Wilson on Aderoju. The loss left newly promoted Dale, who were heavily beaten at Newport in their first game in the EFL since 2023, still searching for their first point of the campaign.
